rules: Specific claims regarding years, lap-time gains, technical parameters, and ban reasons must come ONLY from verified research_notes.
Never name real teams, constructors, drivers, circuits, or commercial sponsors in prompts or narration.
Do not display any F1 logo, Formula 1 or FIA wordmarks, team badges, or watermarks.
Narration must remain strictly within the word budget (22-24 words per clip) in English.
Clip 2 must continue seamlessly from clip 1's final frame with a single camera movement without cuts.
End clip 2 on a clean caption-free freeze frame of the innovation.

variables.era_vehicle: late-1970s wedge-shaped Grand Prix race car with slick tyres and a large rear wing
variables.mechanism_details: a central driven hub, curved carbon-fibre fan blades, and perimeter rubber sealing skirts hugging the asphalt
variables.working_action: The fan spins at high speed, pulling atmospheric air from beneath the underfloor and venting it rearward.
variables.effect_visual: Glowing blue low-pressure suction vectors pull the chassis down towards the track surface as high-speed turbulent airflow streams rearward.
variables.parts_list: the central driven fan hub, high-pitch composite rotor blades, protective mesh cowl, drive clutch, and sealed underbody ducts
variables.narration_1: In nineteen seventy-eight, engineers fitted an engine-driven fan at the rear, generating immense suction under the chassis regardless of speed.
variables.narration_2: The enormous ground effect produced unbelievable cornering grip, but rival protests over thrown debris led to an immediate regulatory ban.
